## Q2
Assertion (A): Dendral is an expert system.<br>
Reason (R): The rationality of an agent is not related to its reaction to the environment.

## Q2 - Options
(A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(C) A is true but R is false
(D) A is false but R is true

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q39

Dendral is one of the earliest and most famous expert systems, built to infer molecular structure from mass spectrometry data, so Assertion A is true.

Reason R is false. A rational agent is defined precisely by how well it reacts to its environment. It chooses actions, based on its percept sequence, to maximize its performance measure. Rationality is fundamentally tied to how an agent perceives and responds to its environment, not independent of it.

So A is true but R is false.

## Q3
Which of the following is not a property of a good system for representing knowledge in a particular domain?

## Q3 - Options
(A) Presentation adequacy
(B) Inferential adequacy
(C) Inferential efficiency
(D) Acquisitional efficiency

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q98

The standard properties of a good knowledge representation system, from AI knowledge-representation theory, are representational adequacy (the ability to represent all the kinds of knowledge needed in the domain), inferential adequacy (the ability to derive new knowledge from existing knowledge), inferential efficiency (the ability to incorporate guidance that keeps inference tractable), and acquisitional efficiency (the ability to acquire new knowledge easily).

- **A. Presentation adequacy** — not a recognized property. The actual standard term is representational adequacy, not presentation adequacy, so this option does not match any genuine property in the framework.
- **B. Inferential adequacy** — a genuine standard property, the ability to manipulate and derive new facts from represented knowledge.
- **C. Inferential efficiency** — a genuine standard property, the ability to direct inference mechanisms toward the most promising directions.
- **D. Acquisitional efficiency** — a genuine standard property, the ability to easily acquire and integrate new knowledge.

Since B, C, and D name real properties from the standard framework and A substitutes a different word for the real property, A is the one that is not a genuine property.

## Q4
What is the process of capturing inference process as a single inference rule?

## Q4 - Options
(A) Ponens
(B) Clauses
(C) Generalized modus ponens
(D) Variables

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q37

Generalized modus ponens combines unification with the classical modus ponens inference pattern into one single rule, letting a reasoning system match implication antecedents against known facts and derive conclusions in one step rather than through several separate logical operations.

This is why it is described as capturing an entire multi-step inference process as one rule, distinguishing it from plain modus ponens, individual clauses, or variables, none of which describe this combined single-rule mechanism.

## Q5
The 4Ws problem canvas helps in identifying the key elements related to the problem. 4Ws problem canvas is a part of \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.

## Q5 - Options
(A) Problem scoping
(B) Data acquisition
(C) Data modeling
(D) Problem Evaluation

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q39

The 4Ws problem canvas, who, what, where, and why, is a structured framework used at the very first stage of the AI project cycle to clearly define the problem before any data collection or modeling begins.

This initial stage of identifying and framing the problem using the 4Ws is what the AI project cycle terms problem scoping, distinguishing it from the later stages of data acquisition, data modeling, and evaluation, which all happen only after the problem itself has been scoped.

## Q6
Consider the following drawbacks of a Rule based approach:

A. The learning is static.<br>
B. Any changes made to the original data will not be considered.<br>
C. Once trained the model cannot improve on the basis of feedback.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q6 - Options
(A) All the above statements are correct
(B) The statements A & B only are not correct
(C) The statements B & C only are not correct
(D) All the above statements are not correct

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q64

A rule-based system operates entirely on a fixed set of hand-coded rules, with no mechanism to learn or adjust those rules from experience.

- **A. The learning is static** — true. A rule-based system cannot adapt its own reasoning over time.
- **B. Changes to the original data are not considered** — true. The system does not automatically pick up on changes in the underlying data the rules were built from.
- **C. The model cannot improve on feedback once trained** — true. There is no feedback loop to improve its behavior after deployment.

All three statements correctly describe genuine limitations of the rule-based approach, so the correct option is that all the above statements are correct.

## Q8
In a database, a rule is defined as (P1 and P2) or P3: R1 (0.8) and R2 (0.3), where P1, P2, P3 are premises and R1, R2 are conclusions of rules with certainty factors (CF) 0.8 and 0.3 respectively. If any running program has produced P1, P2, P3 with CF as 0.5, 0.8, 0.2 respectively, find the CF of results on the basis of premises.

## Q8 - Options
(A) CF (R1 = 0.8), CF (R2 = 0.3)
(B) CF (R1 = 0.40), CF (R2 = 0.15)
(C) CF (R1 = 0.15), CF (R2 = 0.35)
(D) CF (R1 = 0.8), CF (R2 = 0.35)

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q1

Certainty factor rules combine premises before scaling by the rule's own CF.

For an AND premise, CF(P1 and P2) = min(CF(P1), CF(P2)) = min(0.5, 0.8) = 0.5<br>
For an OR premise, the combined premise strength is max(CF(P1 and P2), CF(P3)) = max(0.5, 0.2) = 0.5

Each conclusion then scales this combined premise CF by its own rule CF.<br>
CF(R1) = 0.5 × 0.8 = 0.40<br>
CF(R2) = 0.5 × 0.3 = 0.15

This gives CF(R1 = 0.40) and CF(R2 = 0.15).

## Q11
According to Dempster-Shafer theory for uncertainty management, where Bel(A) denotes Belief of event A:

## Q11 - Options
(A) Bel(A) + Bel(¬A) ≤ 1
(B) Bel(A) + Bel(¬A) ≥ 1
(C) Bel(A) + Bel(¬A) = 1
(D) Bel(A) + Bel(¬A) = 0

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2019 (4 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q25

In Dempster-Shafer theory, belief represents the total support committed to an event based on evidence:

- Unlike classical probability where P(A) + P(¬A) = 1, Dempster-Shafer theory allows uncommitted belief mass due to incomplete knowledge or ignorance.
- Consequently, Bel(A) + Bel(¬A) ≤ 1, with equality holding only when there is complete certainty and zero unassigned belief mass.
- Plausibility Pl(A) relates to belief by Pl(A) = 1 - Bel(¬A), so Bel(A) ≤ Pl(A), which directly confirms Bel(A) + Bel(¬A) ≤ 1.

## Q13
Which of the following is true for semi-dynamic environment ?

## Q13 - Options
(A) Environment and performance score, both change simultaneously.
(B) The environment may change while the agent is deliberating.
(C) The environment itself does not change with the passage of time but the agent’s performance score does.
(D) Even if the environment changes with the passage of time while deliberating, the performance score does not change.

## Q13 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q1

A semi-dynamic environment is formally defined as one where the environment itself does not change while the agent is deliberating, but the agent's performance score decreases or changes with the passage of time.

- In a fully dynamic environment, the physical world state changes while the agent ponders its move.
- In a static environment, neither the environment nor the performance score changes during deliberation.
- In a semi-dynamic environment (such as timed chess), the board state remains frozen until a move is made, but the clock runs down, altering the performance evaluation.
- Therefore, Option C accurately captures the definition of a semi-dynamic environment.

## Q14
An agent can improve its performance by

## Q14 - Options
(A) Responding
(B) Perceiving
(C) Observing
(D) Learning

## Q14 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** AI: Knowledge Representation, Planning & Expert Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Dec 2018 (20 Dec, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q28

In artificial intelligence, an agent improves its future performance specifically through its learning component.

- In a learning agent architecture, the learning element takes feedback from the critic and modifies the performance element to produce better decisions over time.
- Responding (Option A) is executing actions based on current rules.
- Perceiving (Option B) and observing (Option C) provide raw sensory inputs from the environment but do not by themselves modify or improve agent performance.
